properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Beech Resources Llc in Lycoming Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-24 to Beech Resources Llc in Lycoming Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Beech Resources Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-24
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 878007
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: On February 24, 2020 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an inspection for a reported spill (CTS at 348187) at Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. At the time of inspection, the operator was in the process of rigging down the site from the recent stimulation of the wells onsite. The DEP met with Don Stevenson of Beech Resources. He explained that some hoses were disconnected from the blender and were not drained of production fluid. The hoses were not completely placed on containment and spilled about 30 gallons of brine water outside of containment. The operator was in the process of vacuuming the containment. Once that has been completed the containment will be removed and the excavation of the impacted area will begin. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect biased samples of the impacted area. DEP conducted field screening of the puddles in the area where the hoses spilled the brine water for conductivity. The puddles tested returned an over range reading of the conductivity meter (>19.99 mS/cm). Beech Resources plans to excavate the impacted soil to below a soil conductivity of 1000 uS/cm. February 25, 2020 The DEP received an email from Don Stevenson with pictures showing the excavation of the impacted area from the spill the evening of 2/24/2020. The DEP followed up with a site visit to confirm the excavation. At the time of the visit, Penn E&R was onsite continuing the conductivity delineation of the spill. The operator was also continuing to excavate impacted soil from the spill. The area that has been excavated is about a 20' x 30' area at a depth of less than a foot. Penn E&R stated that five 10 yard roll off dumpsters have been filled with impacted soil to this point. More excavation is going to be required to remove the remaining impacted soil. The DEP screened the area of the spill, which resulted in a range of 200 uS/cm to areas that were over range of the meter(>4.00 mS/cm). Before leaving the well pad, the DEP spoke with Don Stevenson on the phone and explained with the area excavated and the amount of impacted soil collected that the DEP recommends starting the Act 2 process. The spill of production fluid from the hoses outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8183690
Permit API: 129-28483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/16/2024
Comments: On April 16th, 2024 the Department conducted a routine inspection of EQT's Cook Well Pad located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying in today's inspection is Samantha Foulk (WQSS DEP).At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road and the ERP was present in the onsite mailbox.There are 2 total wells on this well pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H's well tag as present at the time of inspection with all necessary information posted and no fluid discharges were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers but was not in secondary containment. Well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 promulgation of Chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. Staining of the gravel below the piping of the 17H GPU was observed. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the edge of the well site along the chainlink fence (0.186 mS) as a background, and then three others were taken at the base of the GPU piping where the discoloration can be seen (0.021 mS, 0.002 mS and 0.013 mS). These readings were comparable to the background and therefore are not indicative of a release.The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. A conductivity reading of the fluid within was 0.158 mS. The production tank appeared to be sound with no observable leaks or discharge. The Department recommends the Operator monitor the secondary containment to ensure that the fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements.The access road and well pad appeared to be stabilized. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site did exhibit concerns. The rear riprap apron appeared to be improperly implemented and/or maintained to adequately prevent channelized flow from forming. Approximately 45-50 feet of channelized flow containing sediment was observed going from the end of the riprap apron outlet to an agricultural field nearby. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the riprap apron outlet to prevent any further erosion from occurring. With the exception of this area of concern, the remainder of the well site appeared to exhibit greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.Prior to leaving the location, the Department notified Operator representative Logan Dominick of the above-noted concern, who responded that they would promptly address it.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 8233563
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. The well is situated approximately 650 feet north-northwest of the complainant’s residence. During the inspection, an updated well record was reviewed. The well was actively producing via the 4-inch production string, with valves on the 7-inch intermediate casing and the 4-inch production string annuls closed at the time of inspection Bubbling was observed in the annular space between the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing. Combustible gas screening using a calibrated gas meter indicated a concentration of 29% LEL (1.4%) in this annulus. According to the well records, both the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing were cemented to surface. The presence of combustible gas in the annulus suggests potential defects in the casing and/or cement integrity. Additionally, no check valve was observed on the production lines exiting the well. To further assess possible migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the wellhead in the cardinal directions, each about 3 feet deep. No detectable levels of combustible gas were found in the slam bar holes at the time of the inspection. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on 05/15/2025 was used for combustible gas screening during the inspection. It is noted that the operator has not responded to or completed the recommended corrective actions outlined in Inspection ID# 3913271. These actions were communicated via certified mail (USPS# 9589 0710 5270 1975 0616 42), sent on 02/13/2025 and received by the operator on 02/19/2025. As a result, the violations identified during this inspection are now being formally imposed on this well.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/24/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/24/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 960278
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/23/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 921784
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/23/2021
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both pads. DEP Environmental Trainee John Rogers and DEP Geoscientist Sam Louderback accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. On Pad B, the sump remains installed where fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) was observed on the pad surface. Fluid is present within the sump approximately two feet below the pad surface. The EC of this fluid is 2.19 mS/cm. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed on or off the pad. In the rock-lined ditch along the northwest edge of the pad, two small puddles of fluid were found which had a petroleum odor and a sheen. I notified the company man of the presence of these puddles before leaving the location. On Pad A, we met with company man Grant Boyd upon arriving on location. He told us that excavation had been done after the previous inspection on the pad near the northeast corner of the well site secondary containment. Multiple puddles were observed in this area during this inspection which had an EC between 3.43 mS/cm and 4.33 mS/cm. An additional puddle was observed along the pad edge within the brush barrier along the side of the pad. This puddle had an EC of 2.09 mS/cm. I took a sample, sample #0718-178, from this puddle and sent it to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Li, Br, and Al. I notified the company man of my findings before leaving the location. In a phone call with Rick Hall on the same day at 13:29, I relayed my observations on both pads to Mr. Hall. He said that he would have the puddles investigated and remediated. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 7/21/2025 at 0920 hours. The weather was 65 degrees F with cloudy skies.Remediation efforts are currently underway. A large pit has been excavated around the 7H well (photo #12) and the impacted material is piled onsite for later removal/disposal (photo #14). Repsol plans to have the wellhead reconstructed and then remedial efforts downslope will begin. The extent of downslope impacts off the western corner of the well pad and along the surface waterline in the adjacent field have been delineated. A temporary berm has been installed in the adjacent field, downslope of impacts, to collect fluids as runoff from precipitation occurs (photo #5). The surface waterline has been removed from the impacted area and from the constructed "corner" berm. Numerous areas of distressed vegetation were observed during this inspection (photos #2, 4, 8, 10 and 11).Resource Environmental (Resource), alongside Repsol's construction contractor, began screening and excavating impacted pad material and soils on Friday, 7/18/2025. Repsol reported that all material field measured at >1.0mS/cm is being recovered and stored for later disposal. Material recovered is being placed into lined residual waste containers which are then being covered prior to site departure. Repsol reported that three trucks are running today for removal of the residual waste containers as they are filled. Resource is screening material/soils every few feet, horizontally and vertically, to guide the excavation efforts.Repsol has Larson Design Group working on designing a more permanent type of land design downslope of the pad in order to continue the collection and recovery of fluids. Repsol plans to have a lined sump constructed within the temporary "corner" berm to continue collecting and recovering fluids. A "supervac" water truck is scheduled to arrive tomorrow morning to finish recovering all of the fluids held within the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin. The DEP recommends the following:-continuing fluids and impacted soils recovery-continuing monitoring nearby streams for potential impacts-continuing soil screening/monitoring to determine the extent of the impacts offsiteViolations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301The DEP departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On May 7, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on August 21, 2019. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3969681, which was conducted in response to an estimated 200 gallon diethylene glycol release to the surface of the well pad. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation was ongoing during the time of IR 3969681.Prior to conducting this inspection, the Department spoke via phone with Range Resources representative Nate Smiell who explained that remediation was completed and confirmation samples were collected in the impacted area, per the cleanup requirements of Act 2.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). Well 2H is equipped with a well tag with no staining or evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be in production (see photos 6 and 7). There are six additional wells onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 5). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 8). Secondary containment has been installed onsite in location of the GPU units (see photo 10). A crane is onsite to move the GPU units into the newly-installed secondary containment (see photos 9 and 11). This is being conducted per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department. The rolloff boxes that were present during the time of IR 3969681 appear to have been removed from site. No visual evidence of any remaining impacted material was observed in the formerly impacted area.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that visual remediation of the impacted area has been successfully completed. However, violations issued from IR 3969681 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of this release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program at the time of this inspection.

Violation ID: 850621

Comments: This administrative inspection documents the receipt of sample results for samples taken on the pad on 4/17/19 and samples taken in the sediment ditch (background and where fluid from the pad entered) and sediment trap outfall taken on 4/18/19.
